content: Human-in-the-loop triage architecture: route by risk-tiered lanes (auto-approve high confidence / flag borderline / escalate low-confidence). Well-calibrated systems keep the human approval queue to roughly 5-10% of volume; a persistently larger queue signals miscalibrated thresholds. Model confidence alone is an unreliable signal -- production systems often combine a trust score with a separate risk/policy flag that can override confidence (e.g., safety-critical categories always escalate regardless of confidence). This validates SPEC.md §4.4's three-tier confidence routing plus the independent safety_hazard hard-override, and suggests the ≤20% human-triage target in §11.2 is a reasonable upper bound (best-in-class is tighter, ~10%).
